AUDIT Claude Opus 5.5 — growth-project-backend#648 @ 81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098 — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

This is the first Opus verdict on #648 (a full audit). #648 closes my lens's C-643-2 on #643: inbox notifications never reached a device. The branch is stacked: it contains #647's commit `3a93fbde` plus this PR's commit `81c52a12` (15 files, +1035/-67), and I read all of `3a93fbde..81c52a12`. The PR body has the T4 tier header and states the stacking honestly. #647's B-647-1 (the recipient's zone is really the schema default) is carried into this branch, and closes when #647 is fixed and this branch is rebased.

Counts: A 0, B 1, C 4.

### What holds up
- **Verification of the starting point.** `createNotification` only inserted rows (`notifications.service.ts:303-353`), so the old `push` twins never reached a device.
- **No double pushes.** Neither `messaging.service.ts` nor the scheduling or booking paths call `pushToUser` or `pushToCoach`, so the new `sendPush` cannot double-send.
- **`PushDeliveryService`:**
  - It never throws.
  - It sends at most once and never retries.
  - It clears a token only when the stored token still matches (`updateMany where { id, expo_push_token: token }`).
  - `InvalidCredentials` keeps the token and sends one operator line per hour, so Android without the FCM key cannot cause an error storm.
  - Receipts are checked 2 minutes or more after the send, from a bounded queue, with retry on the next sweep.
- **Lock-screen privacy.** `lock-screen-copy.ts` never shows message text, weight, check-in or milestone values, or coach-alert text. Booking copy carries only a name and a time. There are no emojis or exclamation marks.
- **Tap routing.** `data.actionScreen` (Messages or NotificationCenter) matches the mobile tap router's allow-list (`src/services/pushNotifications.ts:123-156`).
- **Inbox twins.** `PUSH_TWIN_KINDS` hides stored `push` twins in the list and in both unread counts. Push-only kinds stay visible.
- **Gating.** `sendPush` is gated by `muted` and `<kind>_push`.
- **Wiring.** Only `NotificationsModule` provides `PushDeliveryService` and `NotificationsService`, so DI resolves.

### B: must fix before merge
- **B-648-1: the per-kind throttle silently drops distinct, time-critical pushes.**
  - **The code.** `takeRateSlot` (`push-delivery.service.ts`, the `lastByUserKind` key is `${userId}:${kind}`) lets one push per user per kind through per 60 s. It drops the rest with no retry and no collapse.
  - **Why reminders get lost.** The 1-hour reminder sweep runs every 5 minutes over a 55-65 minute window, and the 24-hour sweep every 15 minutes over a ±15 minute window (`reminder.job.ts`). A coach with back-to-back sessions (for example 10:00 and 10:05, or 30-minute slots for the 24-hour reminder) has both sessions in the same tick. The second session's reminder is throttled, and its `NotificationDeliveryLog` claim is already written, so it is never pushed. Reminders are ON at launch (OR-110-5), so this is a missed reminder on the coach's phone.
  - **Messages are hit too.** `message_received` from client A and then client B within 60 s leaves the coach with no push for B.
  - **The 10-minute cap compounds it.** At most 8 pushes per user per 10 minutes, with nothing exempt, which a coach with many active clients can reach.
  - **The tests encode the drop.** `test/push-delivery.service.spec.ts:167-184`.
  - **Minimal fix:**
    - Key the 60 s throttle on the event, not the kind: `${userId}:${kind}:${deep_link ?? ''}`. The deep link already carries the session or thread id. That still collapses repeats of the same event, for example a burst of messages in one thread.
    - Exempt `booking_reminder_*` from the per-user 10-minute cap, or raise the cap for coaches.
    - Add tests: two 1-hour reminders for different sessions to one coach in the same minute give 2 pushes; two messages in the same thread within 60 s give 1 push; messages from two different threads give 2 pushes.

### C
- **C-648-2: `@Optional()` on `pushDelivery` hides a DI miss.** In `NotificationsService` (constructor) a missing provider makes every `sendPush` silently return `null`. Make it required and stub it in the thin tests. (This is the same pattern as C-640-7 and C-647-2.)
- **C-648-3: booking pushes open the notification list, not the session.** They route to `NotificationCenter`. For a reminder, an Apple-level flow opens the session itself. Add a `SessionDetail` route to the mobile allow-list and send `actionScreen: 'SessionDetail'` with the session id (follow-up with mobile).
- **C-648-4 (outside this diff, but this PR makes it user-visible): quiet hours are never enforced.**
  - Mobile ships a Quiet hours toggle (`src/screens/notifications/NotificationPreferencesScreen.tsx:332-410`, reachable from both navigators).
  - It sends a nested `quietHours` object (`src/services/notificationsApi.ts:300-307`), which the backend DTO's whitelist strips. The backend has flat `quiet_hours_start`/`_end` columns that no sender reads, apart from the nudge engine's own policy.
  - Now that messages, milestones and reminders reach the phone, a user who turned on Quiet hours still gets night pushes.
  - Recommended follow-up: have `sendPush` defer or skip non-reminder kinds inside the user's stored quiet hours, and fix the mobile payload mapping. Operator decision on whether this is needed before launch; my default is yes, for messages, milestones and alerts.
- **C-648-5: receipt state lives in memory, so a deploy drops pending receipts.** The PR states this openly. Tokens are still cleared on a later ticket, so the impact is low. Acceptable for v1.0.

### Evidence
- **CI at `81c52a12`:** all 10 required checks pass (build-and-test, rls-floor-guard, rls-live-tests, mwb-3-live-tests, npm audit, CodeQL JS/TS, Banned cast tokens, build-sbom, danger, Schema parity).
- **Merge order:** merge #647 first; this diff then reduces to `81c52a12`.
- **Method:** these findings come from reading the code at the exact head. No local suite was run, because CI is green at this head. Nothing was pushed.

AUDIT GPT-6.1 Sol — growth-project-backend#648 @ 81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098 — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

First Sol verdict on this PR/head; full stacked diff reviewed, including all 15 files in the push-delivery commit after #647. Open **A/B/C: 0/5/0**: three push-delivery Bs plus two inherited Sol Bs from #647. The T4 header correctly identifies device delivery, personal lock-screen content, token writes, and installed-build inbox behavior; all ten required checks pass at this head. [PR contract](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/648), [exact-head checks](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/648/checks).

### Earlier lens findings / what is now proved

The missing dispatcher in Sol B-643-1 is mechanically addressed: the real BookingEmitter now writes one inapp row and calls the preference-gated real sender; the new integration suite proves one push per eligible participant and zero pushes when opted out/muted. Its release outcome remains blocked by B-648-1/B-648-6 below. [Emitter:245-261](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/src/notifications/emitters/booking.emitter.ts#L245-L261), [real-service boundary tests:401-425](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/test/push-delivery.service.spec.ts#L401-L425).

Sol B-643-2's ordinary duplicate/unread case is covered for newly canonical and stored twin rows, but the kind-only historical filter introduces B-648-7 below; recipient-local copy improves C-643-1, but its provenance problem remains inherited B-647-2. [Twin tests:427-460](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/test/push-delivery.service.spec.ts#L427-L460), [Sol #647 verdict](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/647#issuecomment-5963226720).

Token clearing uses an exact-token compare-and-set, provider-credential failures preserve tokens with bounded operator alerts, and receipts are delayed rather than polled immediately. These are substantive improvements, not evidence that every failure boundary is closed. [Sender:159-240](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/src/notifications/push/push-delivery.service.ts#L159-L240).

### B — must fix before merge

**B-648-1 — independently confirmed; retain the existing Opus ID: distinct reminders/messages are silently dropped by the per-kind throttle.** The key is only `(user,kind)`, allowing one per minute, with a blanket eight-per-ten-minute cap. The reminder job can select multiple distinct sessions for the same coach in one window, records each durable claim before dispatch, then receives a normal emitter completion even when the second device push is rate-limited; future sweeps skip that reminder. [Throttle:257-275](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/src/notifications/push/push-delivery.service.ts#L257-L275), [claim-before-emit:118-155](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/src/scheduling/jobs/reminder.job.ts#L118-L155), [existing finding](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/648#issuecomment-5963222971).

**Minimal fix:** separate event deduplication from anti-spam policy: carry a stable event/session/thread identity, avoid collapsing distinct booking reminders or distinct conversations, and use an explicit bounded delivery/coalescing policy instead of permanently losing claimed critical reminders at the blanket cap. Test two due sessions for one coach in the same sweep, same-event repeats, two different threads, and cap behavior for critical reminders. The present test asserts the dropping policy rather than these product outcomes. [Current rate test:167-184](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/test/push-delivery.service.spec.ts#L167-L184).

**B-648-6 — new: external push/receipt awaits have no application-level deadline and now hold committed booking responses and serial reminder delivery open.** The default client is `new Expo()` with no configured delivery deadline; both send and receipt fetch are directly awaited. `sendPush` awaits deliver, BookingEmitter awaits sendPush after writing the inbox item, and scheduling awaits that emitter after the session mutation. Catching a rejected promise does not bound a stalled provider request. [Client/send/receipt awaits:91-174](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/src/notifications/push/push-delivery.service.ts#L91-L174), [service:409-425](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/src/notifications/notifications.service.ts#L409-L425), [booking boundary:178-201](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/src/scheduling/scheduling-session-lifecycle.service.ts#L178-L201).

A stalled Expo send can therefore leave a successfully saved booking looking failed/timed out to its caller and hold later participants in the serial sweep; a stalled receipt fetch holds `receiptSweepRunning` until it settles. **Minimal fix:** impose an explicit small, abortable total transport deadline for sends and receipt fetches, returning the typed transport outcome without invalidating tokens or retrying unknown sends; alternatively decouple the request through a bounded delivery/outbox worker with its own deadline. Do not merely race a timer while leaving the underlying network operation running. Add pending-transport tests proving the booking call and next participant finish within the budget, the transport is canceled, and receipt sweeping releases its latch. Current transport coverage rejects immediately, not after a never-settling/stalled operation. [Serial dispatch:128-156](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/src/scheduling/jobs/reminder.job.ts#L128-L156), [receipt latch:161-195](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/src/notifications/push/push-delivery.service.ts#L161-L195), [immediate-failure test:156-164](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/test/push-delivery.service.spec.ts#L156-L164).

**B-648-7 — new: historical-twin filtering also hides legitimate sole push-channel notifications.** `INBOX_HIDES_PUSH_TWINS` removes every push row of a listed kind from both inbox and unread counts without checking whether an inapp twin exists or whether this writer produced a twin. The coach-AI materializer accepts any free-text kind, defaults to push, and creates exactly one notification with `ai_draft_id`; a coach-approved `message_received` or `checkin_submitted` therefore disappears even when it is the only artifact. The PR body acknowledges this newly introduced hiding; declaring it outside scope does not make the regression pre-existing. [Filter/list/count:70-89,440-470,538-540](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/src/notifications/notifications.service.ts), [accepted payload:58-65](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/src/ai/gateway/materialisers/send-notification.materialiser.ts#L58-L65), [sole-row writer:131-149](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/src/ai/gateway/materialisers/send-notification.materialiser.ts#L131-L149), [acknowledged case](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/648).

**Minimal fix:** hide only proven duplicate rows using provenance/dedup identity or a verified canonical counterpart; at minimum preserve coach-AI rows with `ai_draft_id` and do not assume kind implies a twin. Add a real materializer-to-inbox/count regression with a sole push row using a listed kind, alongside the existing genuine twin case. The current push-only test uses an unlisted kind and cannot detect this loss. [Present test:427-460](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/blob/81c52a1292a620df7dc4389849372983005e4098/test/push-delivery.service.spec.ts#L427-L460).

**B-647-1 and B-647-2 — inherited Sol blockers, not new or renumbered findings.** This candidate still contains #647's unconditional reminder-claim deletion without stale-snapshot fencing, and preference-zone precedence without provenance. Resolve the stale-sweep/no-op-reschedule and synthetic-LA zone cases in #647, then incorporate those fixes into #648; merging #647 unchanged would not close either. [Full Sol findings and minimal fixes](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/647#issuecomment-5963226720), [stack contract](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/648).

### Execution / integration boundaries

No new local Jest run is claimed; execution evidence is the ten green exact-head CI checks, while the uncovered cases above are code-derived. No code was pushed, merged, dispatched, or applied to production. [CI](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/648/checks).

Outside this diff: older `pushToUser`/`pushToCoach`, first-payment dispatch, coach-AI's absent dispatcher, and receipt durability remain explicitly separate scope. Android FCM configuration and real-device delivery are operator release evidence, not established by mocked Expo CI; the existing Opus quiet-hours/tap-routing follow-ups also need an explicit launch decision. Recommended default: fix this branch's Bs, incorporate fixed #647, then require device evidence before claiming launch reminders reach both platforms. [Declared boundaries](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/648), [Opus integration findings](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/648#issuecomment-5963222971).

FIX ROUND 2 (B-NOTIF-5, agent 114) — growth-project-backend#648 @ 16294f44b8738698408b6e8c672574c055cdaab8

Open findings at the latest verdicts (both REQUEST CHANGES at 81c52a12): Opus B-648-1, C-648-2, C-648-3, C-648-4, C-648-5; Sol B-648-1, B-648-6, B-648-7, and the inherited Sol B-647-1 / B-647-2. Lane scope adds OR-113-5 (quiet hours 21:00-08:00 in the recipient's zone, non-urgent deferred, urgent bypass) and "no Android delivery claim without the FCM V1 key".

Design change: every device push is one row in a durable `PushOutbox` (migration `20270307000000_push_outbox_quiet_hours`, forced RLS, anon/authenticated denied, service_role bypass, FK cascade from User). `sendPush` writes the row (in the caller's transaction when given) and returns; a worker leases due rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and sends with a cancelling deadline.


Design change: every device push is now one row in a durable `PushOutbox`. `sendPush` writes the row (in the caller's transaction when there is one) and returns; a worker leases due rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and sends them with a cancelling deadline. Nothing in a request waits on Expo.

| Finding | Change | Commit | Test (fails on 81c52a12) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opus+Sol B-648-1: the per-kind throttle dropped distinct reminders and messages; the 8 / 10 min cap dropped pushes | No in-memory throttle. A booking event has an exactly-once `dedupe_key` (kind, session, start time), so two sessions never collide and two replicas never double-send. Repeats in one conversation collapse (an unsent push takes the newest copy; a repeat within 60 s of a sent one folds into it; the inbox row is still written). The per-user cap (8 per 10 min) now DEFERS non-urgent pushes to when the window has room; booking events are exempt. Nothing is dropped by a rate limit. | de2a78fc | `test/push-delivery.service.spec.ts` "two 1 h reminders for different sessions ... both pushed", "the same reminder enqueued twice ... pushed once", "two messages in the same thread within 60 s give one push; two threads give two", "past the burst cap ... deferred ..., then sent", "urgent reminders are exempt from the burst cap" |
| Sol B-648-6: no deadline on Expo calls; the booking call and the serial sweep waited on Expo | `sendPush` only enqueues. `FetchExpoPushClient` calls the two documented Expo endpoints with a caller-owned AbortSignal (`expo-server-sdk`'s client takes none); sends abort at 10 s, receipt fetches at 15 s, and the request is really cancelled. A timed-out send is not retried (Expo may have accepted it: at most once). HTTP 429/5xx (not accepted) retries with backoff (30 s, 2 min) up to 3 attempts. A row left `sending` by a dead process is closed at lease expiry, never re-sent. | de2a78fc | "sendPush returns while the Expo send never settles; the stalled send is aborted at the deadline", "a stalled receipt fetch is aborted and releases the sweep latch", "HTTP 503 ... retried with backoff, then dropped after MAX_ATTEMPTS", "the fetch transport passes the signal and classifies HTTP errors", "a row left `sending` by a dead process is closed at lease expiry" |
| Sol B-648-7: the kind-only twin filter hid sole push rows (coach-AI) | `Notification.inbox_hidden`. Only a proven twin is hidden: the three writers that store a twin (first payment, drip, purchase fan-out) pass `push_twin: true`; the migration backfills stored twins (a `push` row within 10 s of an `inapp` row with the same user, kind, deep link and text, never a coach-AI row). The inbox and both unread counts filter `inbox_hidden = false`. | de2a78fc | "B-648-7: a proven push twin is hidden; a sole push row of a listed kind stays visible" |
| Opus C-648-4 / OR-113-5: quiet hours not enforced | 21:00-08:00 in the recipient's zone (`resolveRecipientTimeZone`, provenance from #647), one window definition (`QuietHoursPolicy`). Non-urgent pushes wait until 08:00 local. Urgent bypass: the 1 h reminder, and any booking event whose session (old or new time) starts before 08:00 local + 2 h. A deferred reminder is re-checked when sent (session still scheduled at that time, still ahead) and its lock-screen line is rendered then ("today"). No known zone: sent now, never guessed. | de2a78fc | "a message at 23:00 New York waits until 08:00 New York; Tokyo (noon) is sent now", "urgent bypass ...", "a deferred 24 h reminder is re-rendered at 08:00 ("today"), and dropped if the session was cancelled" |
| Opus C-648-5: receipts in memory | Receipts are read from the outbox rows (`ticket_id`, `sent_at`, `receipt_checked_at`) 2+ minutes after the send, so a restart loses none. Rows are deleted after 30 days. | de2a78fc | "receipts survive a restart: a new process reads them from the outbox and clears a dead token" |
| Opus C-648-2: `@Optional()` push delivery hid a DI miss | `NotificationsService.onModuleInit` throws in production when PushDeliveryService is missing (logs an error elsewhere). Thin unit tests that build the service by hand never run the hook. | de2a78fc | "C-648-2: a production boot without PushDeliveryService fails loudly" |
| Android without the FCM V1 key | `InvalidCredentials` keeps the token and records the push as `provider-not-configured`, never as sent; one `PUSH_PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED` line per hour per process. iOS is unaffected. No Android delivery is claimed until the owner uploads the key. | de2a78fc | "InvalidCredentials keeps the token, never records the push as sent, and alerts once an hour" |
| Inherited Sol B-647-1 / B-647-2, Opus B-647-1, C-647-2, C-647-3 | Closed in #647 (head df4eb80b) and merged here. | ee66b618, 9f560fa8 | see #647 FIX ROUND 3 |
| #608 erasure manifest (main ec911328) | `PushOutbox.user_id` erased with the account (`del`, FK-safe: child of User, cascades). | 16294f44 | `test/account-deletion/erasure-manifest-coverage.spec.ts` (failed before with `PushOutbox.user_id` uncovered), `manifest-fk-order.spec.ts` |
| Opus C-648-3: booking pushes open the list, not the session | Backend half: push `data` now carries `sessionId` next to the deep link. The tap still targets `NotificationCenter` because the mobile allow-list has no session screen yet; a `SessionDetail` route is a mobile follow-up. | de2a78fc | n/a (data field only; the tap target change is mobile) |

Kept from round 1: lock-screen privacy (no health detail, no message text), exact-token compare-and-set clearing, preference gating (`muted`, `<kind>_push`), one inbox row per event, emitters wired.
